title: Martin wins red-flagged Nürburgring opener
dek: Maxime Martin won Race 1 from second on the grid, 2.543 seconds clear of Edoardo Mortara, after a first-lap red flag and a late Mortara-Spengler clash handed Pascal Wehrlein third.

chapters.title: Wehrlein arrives with the title in his hands
text: The DTM came to the Nürburgring for the eighth of its nine race weekends with Pascal Wehrlein in control of the championship. The Mercedes driver led on 140 points, 14 ahead of Mattias Ekström and 30 clear of Edoardo Mortara, with Jamie Green on 107, Bruno Spengler on 104 and Marco Wittmann on 98. The previous round at Oschersleben had been a BMW clean sweep, with the marque winning both races and filling all six podium places, and the performance weights had been reshuffled again for the Eifel. Wehrlein's Mercedes was now the heaviest car in the field at 1,130kg, while the lightest cars, at 1,112.5kg, were the BMWs of Maxime Martin and Martin Tomczyk and the Audi of Adrien Tambay.

The two Nürburgring races were the 15th and 16th of the season's 18, so only four remained, these two and two more in the Hockenheim finale in October, so 100 points were still on offer and Wehrlein's 14-point cushion over Ekström was worth less than a single win. Saturday's race was the shorter of the weekend's two, a 40-minute sprint; Sunday's longer race would include a compulsory pit stop. For Audi's pair of Ekström and Mortara the weekend was a chance to eat into the gap, and for Wehrlein a chance to stretch it.

chapters.title: Rookie Auer takes a surprise pole
text: Lucas Auer, one of Mercedes' two rookies, took pole with a lap of 1m21.915s, 0.084s quicker than Maxime Martin's BMW and the first pole of his DTM career. Wehrlein qualified third on 1m22.030s, with Spengler's BMW only two thousandths of a second behind in fourth. Mortara was the best of the Audis in fifth, sharing the third row with Maximilian Götz, the other Mercedes rookie, who had set 1m22.072s. Green was seventh, Mike Rockenfeller eighth, Daniel Juncadella ninth and Miguel Molina tenth, so the first ten cars were covered by just 0.206s.

The championship contenders were split. Wehrlein's third place was easily the best of them, because Ekström, his closest pursuer in the table, managed only 17th on 1m22.372s. Gary Paffett was 14th, Wittmann 12th, and the Oschersleben winners had a poor session: Tom Blomqvist qualified 11th and Timo Glock 18th. Paul di Resta, Tambay and Tomczyk set no time, and technical problems kept Tomczyk's BMW out of both qualifying and the race.

chapters.title: Contact at Turn 1, then a stoppage
text: Wehrlein made the best start of the front runners and went for the lead into Turn 1, but Martin was already on the inside and the two touched. The contact damaged the Mercedes' front-right and Wehrlein dropped to fourth behind Spengler and Mortara, while Auer, who had overbraked at the first corner, slipped back through the field. Further back, a three-wide moment at Turn 3 turned Green's Audi around and Molina ran into it; Timo Scheider's Audi was clipped as well, and Green and Molina were out on the spot.

With debris and oil on the track the safety car came out and the race was red-flagged, the cars lining up on the pit straight. Wehrlein climbed out of his Mercedes, walked to Martin's BMW and hammered on the driver's window. Martin, who said he had been on the inside, called it a racing incident. The race was restarted behind the safety car with 30 minutes on the clock.

chapters.title: Mortara and Wehrlein go through on Spengler
text: Martin pulled clear of the field straight after the restart, and for much of the race Spengler's BMW ran second ahead of Mortara and Wehrlein without being able to stay with the leader. Around lap 15 Mortara dived down the inside of Spengler at Turn 1. The two touched, and Wehrlein, who had been following, went through as well to take third.

Spengler fought on in a damaged car with the rivals queuing behind him, but a puncture sent him into the pits and he lost seven laps, ending up classified 19th. Wehrlein then chased Mortara for the rest of the race without finding a way past. Blomqvist and Scheider both dropped out, after nine and 11 laps respectively, Scheider with the damage from the opening-lap incident.

chapters.title: Martin wins, Wehrlein extends his lead
text: Martin took the flag after 25 laps in 48m17.036s, 2.543s ahead of Mortara, for his second DTM win and his first of 2015. Wehrlein was 0.412s further back in third. Martin also set the fastest lap, a 1m23.502s on lap 7.

Paffett had climbed from 14th on the grid to fourth, passing Götz late on, and Götz held fifth ahead of Auer, who recovered to sixth after losing the lead at the start. Wittmann was seventh, Robert Wickens eighth and António Félix da Costa ninth. Ekström collected a single point for tenth after starting 17th. Wehrlein, who had apologised to Martin after watching the replay and conceding that the BMW driver had simply used a gap, left with 155 points. Mortara moved up to second on 128, one point ahead of Ekström, which put Wehrlein 27 points clear with 75 still available.

facts.v: Maxime Martin won over 25 laps in 48m17.036s, 2.543s ahead of Edoardo Mortara and 2.955s ahead of Pascal Wehrlein.
